transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that over the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always doing something. Puttering around the house, fixing things, rearranging things, saying yes to one more volunteer task. Even at my age, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.
Do you find it hard to relax or sit still even when you want to, or do you feel restless most of the time?

Yes, I do. Like when I’m at the senior center meetings, or even sitting through the announcements at church, I get this ants-in-my-chair feeling. I’ll keep shifting around, or I’ll get up for coffee, or straighten papers—just something to get through sitting there.

Have you had periods where you felt unusually happy, full of energy, or so good that you hardly needed sleep, or found yourself getting involved in lots of activities that could have serious consequences, like spending sprees or risky projects?
No, I don’t think so. I have plenty of energy sometimes, but not like feeling unusually high or needing no sleep. And I haven’t been doing things like spending sprees or risky projects.
Do you often feel irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you can't keep busy or when someone interrupts what you're doing?
I don’t think I’m especially irritable, no. I can get a little bothered if I’m interrupted, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed it being a big problem.
When you do find yourself resting or having downtime, do you ever feel unusually tired or as if you have no energy at all?
Not really, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone my age, especially later in the day, but I don’t usually feel like I have no energy at all when I’m resting.
Have there been times when you felt like you needed much less sleep than usual, but still had plenty of energy?
No, I can’t say that’s happened. If I don’t sleep well, I usually notice it the next day. I don’t have times where I need hardly any sleep and still feel full of energy.
Have there been times when your thoughts seemed to race through your head so fast that it was hard to keep up, or when one idea quickly led to another and you couldn’t slow your thinking down?
No, I don’t think so. My mind can wander sometimes, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts race so fast I can’t keep up with them.
Have there been times when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?
I don’t think so. I have my low days now and then, but not where I felt depressed or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for two weeks.
Have there been times when your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or you felt unusually good and confident for several days in a row, even if it didn’t last very long?
No, I don’t think so. I can get irritated like anyone, but not in a way where my mood is unusually high or I feel overly confident for several days.
Have there ever been a time when your mood was so consistently upbeat, excited, or elevated for a few days or more that others might have noticed it, even if you felt it was normal at the time?
No, I can’t think of a time like that. I’ve had good moods, of course, but not where I was unusually upbeat or excited for days and other people noticed.

Have there ever been times when you felt so good, energetic, or excited that you were doing a lot more than usual—like taking on extra projects, being more social, or feeling like you didn’t need much rest?

Not like feeling unusually good or excited, no. It’s more that this past year I just seem to always be puttering around—fixing things, arranging things, signing up to help with one more thing. Even at my age, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.
Have there been times when your mood was noticeably more upbeat, excited, or irritable for several days in a row, even if it didn’t last very long or seem extreme to you at the time?
No, I don’t believe so. I have ordinary ups and downs, and I can get irritated at times, but I haven’t noticed any stretch of several days where my mood was unusually upbeat or irritable like that.

Have there ever been times when your mood was elevated, expansive, or irritable for at least several days in a row—like feeling unusually good, wired, or easily annoyed—where it was a noticeable change from your usual self, even if it didn't seem extreme at the time?
No, I don’t think so. I can get annoyed like anyone, but not for several days in a way that felt like a real change from how I usually am. Nothing like feeling wired or unusually good for days.
Have there been times when you found your attention being easily drawn to things around you—like sounds, sights, or thoughts—so much so that it was hard to stay focused on what you were doing?

I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that in a big way. I mean, things can catch my attention like they would for anyone, but I can’t say sounds or sights pull me away so much that I can’t stay with what I’m doing.

Have there ever been a few days or more when your mood was clearly different from usual—like feeling unusually good, wired, or easily annoyed—where it was noticeable enough that someone close to you might have commented on it, even if it didn’t seem extreme to you at the time?
No, I don’t think anyone close to me has ever pointed out something like that. I’ve had normal moods, good days and irritable moments, but not a few days where I seemed really different or wired.
Over the past year, have you had days where you felt driven to keep moving or doing things, like you couldn't slow yourself down, and this happened almost every day?

Yes. That’s actually a lot of why I came in. For the past year or so, I feel like I’m always puttering around—fixing something, arranging things, signing up to help with one more thing. Even at my age, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.
When you've been feeling driven to keep moving or doing things almost every day, did you also feel that you needed much less sleep than usual, even though you still had plenty of energy?
I don’t think so. I mean, my sleep isn’t perfect, but I haven’t noticed needing much less sleep and still feeling full of energy. That doesn’t really sound like what’s been happening.
When you've been feeling driven to keep moving or doing things almost every day, did you also find yourself taking on a lot more activities, projects, or social commitments than you normally would?

Yes, I’d say so. It’s not big dramatic projects, but I’m always finding one more thing to do—fixing something around the house, rearranging things, or volunteering to help with something. I just have a hard time sitting down and leaving things alone.
